newsitem.title: USA: Tribune trims Renaissance dilution view.
newsitem.headline: Tribune trims Renaissance dilution view.

text.p: Tribune Co expects earnings dilution in 1997 of about seven percent, rather than the 10 percent projected previously, from its pending $1.13 billion acquisition of Renaissance Communications Corp, company officials told analysts in a teleconference Friday.
"That's our best guess," Tribune spokesman Robert Carr told Reuters.
Last July Tribune announced plans to acquire Renaissance, which owns six television stations.
Tribune executives said in the teleconference that Renaissance is expected to add more in operating earnings than interest costs, but goodwill amortization will cause dilution.

Tribune, reporting higher fourth quarter results Friday, said its broadcasting and entertainment operating revenues were flat in the quarter but were up six percent for the full year due to acquisitions of stations in Houston and San Diego.
In the teleconference, Tribune officials said the company was looking for 1997 revenues in its broadcast group, including Renaissance, to rise 25 to 30 percent.

On the newspaper side, it is targeting revenue growth of two to four percent, similar to the growth achieved in 1996, they said. The media company is assuming a 10-15 percent decline in average year-over-year newsprint costs, they said.
The comments of Tribune officials were relayed to Reuters by analysts who took part in the teleconference. The comments were confirmed by Tribune spokesmen.
